Survivorship Bias in Backtests: Why Missing Dead Stocks Flatter Performance

Historical stock and fund databases often contain only the entities that survived to the present, quietly omitting companies that went bankrupt, were delisted, or were acquired. This article explains the mechanics of survivorship bias, why it inflates backtested performance, why value-oriented strategies are especially exposed, and what questions to ask about any published track record.

The Same Bias in Mutual Fund and Hedge Fund Data
